newsitem.title: PERU: Peru mudslide kills 33 villagers, 100 missing.
newsitem.headline: Peru mudslide kills 33 villagers, 100 missing.

text.p: Thirty-three people were killed and at least 100 were missing when an Andean mountainside collapsed on Tuesday, sending a wall of mud slamming into two Peruvian villages, authorities said.
"We have recovered 33 bodies at this point. That is confirmed," Luis Barra Pacheco, mayor of the region's capital, Abancay, told Reuters. "Under the mud, there are at least 100 people."
Rescuers and officials returning from the scene in the southeastern zone of Apurimac told Reuters they had pulled dozens of bodies from the mud and seen many mutilated corpses.

"There were arms, heads, pieces of bodies sticking out of the mud," firefighter Richard Rojas told Reuters by telephone after returning to Abancay from the site. "We have tried to dig up the bodies using picks and shovels, but it's been difficult."
Rescuers said the corpses had been battered and mutilated by stones carried in the torrent of mud.
The mudslide occurred at about 4 a.m. (0900 GMT), virtually burying the villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra, near Abancay, which were home to nearly 250 people.
"Two villages have totally disappeared," Barra Pacheco said, adding an estimated 10.5 million cubic feet (300,000 cubic metres) of mud slid off the mountain.

Police officials said the villages had been evacuated prior to the mudslide after flooding over the weekend. But their refuge in a fold of the mountain just above their homes put them squarely in the path of the mud as it tumbled down on Monday.
Area legislator Dennis Vargas Marin called on President Alberto Fujimori's government to declare a state of emergency.

"As a congressman I ask that the city of Abancay and its surrounding districts be declared in a state of emergency," he told local radio. He estimated up to 300 people may have disappeared and warned of more potential disasters if the torrential rains continued.

Fujimori met with his Cabinet in the afternoon to discuss the mudslide and the hostage crisis at the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence, where Marxist rebels were holding 72 hostages for the 63rd day.
The Civil Defence said it was sending 18 tonnes of supplies to the region for survivors, three dogs to help rescuers and a geologist to assess further risks.

Local police said reports from villagers indicated 50 to 60 families were buried, with 14 bodies recovered from Ccocha. They faxed a list to Reuters with the names of 83 villagers reported missing, and seven bodies that had been identified.
Alejandro Caballero, mayor of the neighbouring village of Tamburco, said he believed there were more than 200 people missing. "No one has survived there," he said.
Flash floods, mudslides and landslides are common in Peru's Andes during the January-March rainy season.

Over the weekend, five people died in flooding in the town of Tamburco, also in Apurimac, while floods in the jungle province of Rioja destroyed the homes of 500 families and swept away a woman and two children in the village of Yuracyacu.
